'''David Parker''' {{post-nominals|FRS|FRSC|country=GBR|size=100%}} (born 30 July 1956)<ref name="whoswho">{{Who's Who|author=Anon|title=Parker, Prof. David|id=U42978|year=2023|doi=10.1093/ww/9780199540884.013.U42978|edition=online [[Oxford University Press]]|location=Oxford}}</ref> is an English chemist who is Chair Professor at [[Hong Kong Baptist University]], and [[Emeritus|Emeritus Professor]] at [[Durham University]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title = David Parker (0000-0001-5281-5146) – ORCID {{!}} Connecting Research and Researchers|url = http://orcid.org/0000-0001-5281-5146|publisher = orcid.org|access-date = 2015-12-29}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title = Prof. D Parker – Durham University|url = https://www.dur.ac.uk/chemistry/staff/profile/?id=195|publisher = Durham University|access-date = 2015-12-29}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
David Parker was born in Leadgate, [[County Durham]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=8 July 2026 |title=David-Parker-oration.pdf |url=https://www.durham.ac.uk/media/durham-university/professional-services/ceremonies-all/honorary-graduates/2026/David-Parker-oration.pdf |access-date=8 July 2026}}</ref> He grew up in [[Durham, England]] and was educated at [[Durham Johnston School]] and briefly at [[King Edward VI High School, Stafford]].<ref name=whoswho/> Having gained an Open Exhibition to [[Christ Church, Oxford]], he read [[chemistry]] at the [[University of Oxford]], where he gained a [[British undergraduate degree classification|First Class degree]] in 1978, and a [[Doctor of Philosophy|DPhil]] in 1980, working with John Brown FRS,<ref name="adphil">{{cite thesis|degree=DPhil|publisher=University of Oxford|url=https://copac.jisc.ac.uk/id/31680866?style=html|website=jisc.ac.uk|title=Studies in Asymmetric Catalysis|first=David|last=Parker|date=1980|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.279472}}|archive-date=3 September 2018|access-date=3 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180903114715/https://copac.jisc.ac.uk/id/31680866?style=html|url-status=dead}}</ref> based on mechanistic studies in [[Enantioselective synthesis|asymmetric catalysis]].<ref>{{Cite journal|title = Intermediates in the asymmetric hydrogenation of unsaturated carboxylic acid derivatives|journal = Journal of the Chemical Society, Chemical Communications|issue = 8|pages = 342–344|doi = 10.1039/c39800000342|first1 = John M.|last1 = Brown|first2 = David|last2 = Parker|date = January 1980}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|title = The mechanism of asymmetric hydrogenation catalysed by rhodium complexes of chiral pyrrolidinobiphosphines|journal = Journal of Organometallic Chemistry|date = 29 September 1981|pages = 249–260|volume = 218|issue = 2|doi = 10.1016/S0022-328X(00)86107-0|first1 = Kazuo|last1 = Achiwa|first2 = Penny|last2 = A. Chaloner|first3 = David|last3 = Parker}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|title = Mechanism of asymmetric homogeneous hydrogenation. Rhodium-catalyzed reductions with deuterium and hydrogen deuteride|journal = Organometallics|date = 1 May 2002|pages = 950–956|volume = 1|issue = 7|doi = 10.1021/om00067a010|first1 = John M.|last1 = Brown|first2 = David|last2 = Parker}}</ref>

==Career and research==
In 1980, he was appointed to a [[NATO]] Fellowship to work with [[Jean-Marie Lehn]] (Nobel Prize, 1987),<ref>{{Cite journal|title = Interview with David Parker|journal = Chemical Communications|volume = 48|issue = 40|pages = 4797|doi = 10.1039/c2cc90093a|pmid = 22491244|date = 2012-04-23|last1 = Parker|first1 = D.}}</ref> and was appointed to a Lectureship in Chemistry at Durham University, beginning in January 1982. He became Chair Professor of Chemistry at Hong Kong Baptist University in September 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.scmp.com/news/hong-kong/education/article/3220627/39-top-overseas-academics-recruited-under-hong-kong-talent-scheme-some-say-shortage-lab-resources|title=39 top overseas academics recruited under Hong Kong talent scheme, but some say shortage of lab resources, high property costs a deterrent|first=William|last=Yiu|work=[[South China Morning Post]]|date=2023-05-29|access-date=2023-05-29}}</ref>

Parker's research investigates the design and synthesis of chiral functional molecules, materials and conjugates and has straddled the traditional disciplines of [[Physical chemistry|physical]], [[Organic chemistry|organic]] and [[Inorganic chemistry|inorganic]] chemistry. Often collaborating with European and UK industry, Parker has worked on collaborative projects leading to the introduction of imaging<ref>{{Cite journal|title = Critical design issues in the targeted molecular imaging of cell surface receptors|journal = Chem. Soc. Rev.|pages = 2122–2134|volume = 44|issue = 8|doi = 10.1039/c4cs00364k|pmid = 25711408|first1 = Neil|last1 = Sim|first2 = David|last2 = Parker|date = 2015-04-10|doi-access = free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|title = Characterisation and evaluation of paramagnetic fluorine labelled glycol chitosan conjugates for 19F and 1H magnetic resonance imaging|journal = Journal of Biological Inorganic Chemistry|date = 17 August 2013|issn = 0949-8257|pages = 215–227|volume = 19|issue = 2|doi = 10.1007/s00775-013-1028-y|pmid = 23955558|first1 = Elena De|last1 = Luca|first2 = Peter|last2 = Harvey|first3 = Kirsten H.|last3 = Chalmers|first4 = Anurag|last4 = Mishra|first5 = P. Kanthi|last5 = Senanayake|first6 = J. Ian|last6 = Wilson|first7 = Mauro|last7 = Botta|first8 = Marianna|last8 = Fekete|first9 = Andrew M.|last9 = Blamire|s2cid = 1529929|url = http://dro.dur.ac.uk/12932/1/12932.pdf}}</ref> and therapeutic agents,<ref>{{Cite journal|title = Responsive and reactive terbium complexes with an azaxanthone sensitiser and one naphthyl group: applications in ratiometric oxygen sensing in vitro and in regioselective cell killing|journal = Chemical Communications|issue = 47|pages = 7321–7323|doi = 10.1039/b920222f|pmid = 20024215|first1 = Ga-Lai|last1 = Law|first2 = Robert|last2 = Pal|first3 = Lars O.|last3 = Palsson|first4 = David|last4 = Parker|first5 = Ka-Leung|last5 = Wong|date = 2009-11-24}}</ref> including the antibody conjugate [[Gemtuzumab ozogamicin|MyloTarg]].

==Awards and honours==
Parker gained recognition from the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]], being awarded, among other prizes, the [[Corday-Morgan Prize|Corday-Morgan Medal]] (1987),<ref>{{Cite web|title = RSC Corday-Morgan Prize Previous Winners|url = http://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/CordayMorganPrizes/PreviousWinners.asp|publisher = rsc.org|access-date = 2015-12-31}}</ref> Ludwig Mond Medal (2011), the [[Hickinbottom Award]] (1988),<ref>{{Cite web|title = RSC Hickinbottom Award Previous Winners|url = http://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/HickinbottomAward/PreviousWinners.asp|publisher = rsc.org|access-date = 2015-12-31}}</ref> an Interdisciplinary Award (RSC, 1996),<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/InterdisciplinaryPrize/PreviousWinners.asp|title=RSC Interdisciplinary Prize Previous Winners|website=www.rsc.org|language=en|access-date=2018-08-10}}</ref> a [[List of Royal Society of Chemistry medals and awards|Tilden]] Lectureship (2003)<ref>{{Cite web|title = RSC Tilden Prize Previous Winners|url = http://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/TildenPrizes/PreviousWinners.asp|publisher = rsc.org|access-date = 2015-12-31}}</ref> and the [[Ludwig Mond Award|Ludwig Mond]] Prize and Medal (2011).<ref>{{Cite web|title = Ludwig Mond 2011 Award Winner|url = http://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/LudwigMondAward/2011winner.asp|publisher = rsc.org|access-date = 2015-12-31}}</ref> In 2002 he was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] (FRS)<ref>{{Cite web|title = David Parker|url = https://royalsociety.org/people/david-parker-12045/|publisher = royalsociety.org|access-date = 2015-12-31}}</ref> and gained the [[Ludwig Mond Award|ICI Prize]] in Organic Chemistry in 1991 and the [[Paul-Émile Lecoq de Boisbaudran|Lecoq de Boisbaudran]] prize in rare earth science in 2012.<ref>{{Cite web|title = Lecoq de Boisbaudran Award {{!}} icfe|url = http://icfe8.uniud.it/?q=node/28|website = icfe8.uniud.it|access-date = 2015-12-31}}</ref> In 2014, he was made an [[EPSRC]] RISE Fellow, recognising inspiration in science and engineering.<ref>{{Cite web|title = RISE Awards Announced – EPSRC website|url = https://www.epsrc.ac.uk/newsevents/news/riseawards/|website = epsrc.ac.uk|access-date = 2015-12-31}}</ref> He was awarded an honorary [[Doctor of Science|Doctor Of Science]] by Durham University in July 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |last=University |first=Durham |title=Honorary Degrees - Durham University |url=https://www.durham.ac.uk/about-us/professional-services/ceremonies/honorary-degrees/ |access-date=2026-07-08 |website=www.durham.ac.uk |language=en-gb}}</ref>
